verdict.rationale: Activepieces flows are built from a trigger plus actions and fire when activated once published. Its agents handle work as it arrives and carry out the steps themselves, and interrupted runs resume from checkpoints, so automations run autonomously in the background. missing for 10: explicit documentation of trigger types such as schedules or polling (recurring runs are only implied by the 'every morning' agent example), independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended background execution.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Flow consists of two parts, trigger and actions
Actions come after the trigger and control what occurs when the flow is activated
You write down the job in plain language, give it access to the apps it needs, and it handles the work as it arrives.
It decides the steps and carries them out.
Interrupted runs resume from their last checkpoint instead of starting over
Write "summarise my unread emails every morning" and you get a drafted agent
